claim.quote: Allowing for time-variable flux, this constitutes 3.5{\sigma} evidence for neutrino emission from the direction of TXS 0506+056, independent of and prior to the 2017 flaring episode.

date.note: arXiv v1 submission date. Published as Science 361, 147-151 (2018).

name: Evidence for a 2014–2015 neutrino flare from TXS 0506+056

significance.quote: Allowing for time-variable flux, this constitutes 3.5{\sigma} evidence for neutrino emission from the direction of TXS 0506+056, independent of and prior to the 2017 flaring episode.

summary.plain: Looking back through nine and a half years of data, IceCube found that the same blazar had already sent a burst of neutrinos in 2014–15, independently of the 2017 alert.
summary.technical: Archival time-dependent point-source search of 9.5 years of IceCube data at the position of TXS 0506+056 finds an excess between September 2014 and March 2015 at 3.5σ for a time-variable flux hypothesis.

title: Neutrino emission from the direction of the blazar TXS 0506+056 prior to the IceCube-170922A alert
why_it_matters: Independent, archival evidence that blazars are sources of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos.
